source.title: Reverse replay of behavioural sequences in hippocampal place cells during the awake state

confidence_rationale: Canonical biological evidence that the brain propagates reward backward along a just-experienced trajectory via reverse replay -- the exact operation a novelty bonus lacks and the archetype of REE's existing backward_credit_sweep. Grounds the credit-assignment lever; indirect (observational, not an RL benchmark).
failure_signatures: A per-step novelty bonus has no mechanism to propagate a terminal reward backward along the trajectory that earned it; reverse replay is that missing operation.

mapping.source_claim_statement: During awake pauses after spatial experience, hippocampal place-cell sequences replay in reversed order (most-recent-location-first, back toward the start), which the authors suggest plays a role in evaluating event sequences in the manner of reinforcement-learning models.
mapping.ree_translation: Reverse replay is the biological archetype of REE's already-present hippocampal backward_credit_sweep; it validates that the sweep is the faithful primitive for propagating forage reward backward along the visited trajectory -- the credit-assignment half of the floor->competent gap.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Observational neuroscience, not an RL performance result; it grounds the mechanism class and validates existing REE machinery but does not itself measure a floor->competent delta.
mapping.source_context: Rat hippocampal place-cell recordings on a linear track, awake immobility after runs.

confidence_components.notes: Strong biological grounding; the value is that it maps onto machinery REE ALREADY has, so the move is to exercise/strengthen the sweep, not add a parallel novelty mechanism.
